title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
abstract: arXiv:2611.28873v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Action tokenizers let robot policies treat control as autoregressive next-token prediction. As these policies are trained on larger and more diverse datasets, they will need a universal tokenizer that can encode actions from many embodiments and data sources, including ones it has not seen. We study action tokenization at scale, training on 49k hours of action data from real-world robots, handheld grippers, simulation, and humans. We introduce Neural Action Tokenizer (NAT), a causal tokenizer whose decoder lets actions be executed as their tokens are generated. Across four simulation benchmarks, NAT outperforms FAST and prior neural action tokenizers when tokenizing unseen robot embodiments, and in vision-language-action models it outperforms FAST+ across four benchmarks and on a real robot when acting through its tokens. translated_title: NAT：跨具身形态扩展的因果神经动作分词器
translated_abstract: 动作分词器使机器人策略能够将控制视为自回归的下一词元预测。随着这些策略在更大规模、更多样化的数据集上训练，它们将需要一个通用的分词器，能够编码来自多种具身形态和数据源的动作，包括其未曾见过的数据源。我们研究了大规模的动作分词，使用来自真实世界机器人、手持夹爪、仿真环境以及人类的4.9万小时动作数据进行训练。我们提出了神经动作分词器（NAT），这是一种因果分词器，其解码器允许在生成词元的同时执行动作。在四个仿真基准测试中，NAT在对未见过的机器人具身形态进行分词时优于FAST和先前的神经动作分词器；在视觉-语言-动作模型中，NAT在四个基准测试以及真实机器人上通过其词元执行动作时均优于FAST+。在某些基准测试中，NAT词元还缩小了与流匹配动作头之间的性能差距，同时降低了推理[成本]。
tldr: 提出了神经动作分词器NAT——一种基于4.9万小时多源数据训练、可跨具身形态泛化的因果动作分词器，在多个仿真基准和真实机器人上均优于FAST等现有方法。
en_tdlr: NAT is a causal neural action tokenizer trained on 49k hours of multi-source action data that generalizes across embodiments, outperforming FAST and prior neural tokenizers on simulation benchmarks and real robots.
